J1 · Onboarding + privacy promise

State the three promises before asking for anything.

MIRRORSee how you actually use your phoneMirror shows the quality of your attention, not just the hours. It runs on this device and never asks you to log anything by hand.
Your history stays on this phoneTitles, searches and timestamps are stored and analysed locally, encrypted.
Two profiles, never mergedPrivate holds everything. Public holds only the topics you pick, one by one. Nothing is copied across.
No streaks, no guilt, no dark patternsMirror exists to reduce mindless use. It will not nudge you to come back.

A decade of YouTube history can be 50–200 MB in one watch-history.json. Mirror reads one file at a time and refuses a file over 67 million characters (64 MiB) instead of cutting it short.If yours is larger, Mirror says so and asks you to request a shorter date range or split the archive. It will not import part of a file and call the rest empty.
A partial import would make a quiet week look quiet. That is the one failure this screen exists to prevent.
